extracted.intended_audience: poets and creative writers (students, critics, practitioners interested in poetic craft)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing a short poem (illustrated by Poe's composition of 'The Raven'), emphasizing planning, unity of effect, tone (melancholy), refrain usage, stanzaic and sonic choices, and suggestiveness. Useful to writers aiming for a compact, intense lyric-narrative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaborate plot to its dénouement before writing
rubrics_metrics.description: “Every plot, worth the name, must be elaborated to its dénouement before anything be attempted with the pen.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan the ending (dénouement) first so all incidents and tone throughout the work tend toward and causally support that conclusion; this gives the plot an indispensable air of consequence or causation. Avoid constructing a story piecemeal without a known resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commence with a chosen effect (novel and vivid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin by asking: 'Of the innumerable effects... what one shall I, on the present occasion, select?' — choose a novel, vivid effect as the poem's primary aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the single emotional or intellectual impression you want to produce (originality + vividness). Decide whether that effect is best achieved by incident, by tone, or by both; then seek combinations of event and tone to construct that effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep originality foremost and seek it deliberately
rubrics_metrics.description: “Keeping originality always in view... originality... is by no means a matter... of impulse or intuition. In general, to be found, it must be elaborately sought.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek original solutions (often by negation or deliberate selection) rather than relying on impulse. Originality may arise in combinations (e.g., unusual stanzaic combinations) even when individual components are traditional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of impression: limit length to single sitting
rubrics_metrics.description: If any literary work is too long to be read at one sitting, it loses the immensely important effect derivable from unity of impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For poems, prefer lengths readable in one sitting (Poe chose ~100 lines). Brevity should be in direct ratio to intensity of intended effect; overly long poems risk becoming a succession of brief effects and losing totality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Beauty the poem's legitimate province
rubrics_metrics.description: Poe argues that 'Beauty is the sole legitimate province of the poem' — Beauty being an intense, elevating, and pure effect on the soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize creating pleasurable elevation (beauty) over didactic truth or raw passion; if truth or passion are introduced, tone them into subservience to Beauty and veil them so they aid rather than dominate the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose melancholy as the highest poetical tone
rubrics_metrics.description: “This tone is one of sadness... Melancholy is thus the most legitimate of all the poetical tones.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the highest manifestation of Beauty, consider a melancholic tone; melancholy naturally produces intense, elevating responses. Use sadness strategically when it serves the intended poetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a refrain but diversify its application
rubrics_metrics.description: The refrain is universally useful; Poe decided to 'adhere, in general, to the monotone of sound, while I continually varied that of thought' — keeping the refrain itself largely unvaried while varying its application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ a recurring burden/refrain to anchor the poem, but vary the semantic or situational context in which it appears to produce continuously novel effects rather than mere monotony of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select a brief, sonorous refrain (often a single word)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because frequent variation of application is desired, the refrain 'must be brief' — Poe chose a single sonorous word ('Nevermore') with long 'o' plus 'r' for emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer short, highly sonorous refrains that allow protracted emphasis; choose vowel and consonant combinations that sustain sound and match tone (e.g., long 'o' with 'r' for sonority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a plausible pretext for repeated refrain (use non-reasoning agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: To justify continuous repetition, Poe chose a 'non-reasoning creature capable of speech' (a Raven) so the monotony didn't conflict with rational behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building a repeating motif or device, ensure narrative plausibility for its repetition; consider using a non-rational agent or contrivance when repeated, rote utterance would otherwise be implausible for a human character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish the climax (climacteric stanza) first
rubrics_metrics.description: Poe composed the climacteric stanza first so he could 'the better vary and graduate... the preceding queries' and settle rhythm, meter, stanza length, and arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the pivotal moment early in the compositional process to calibrate the intensity, rhythm, and to ensure earlier parts never surpass the climax; you may intentionally weaken subsequent passages to preserve climactic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberately choose meter and stanzaic combination
rubrics_metrics.description: While admitting he used known feet, Poe emphasizes originality 'in their combination into stanza' and employed unusual effects from rhyme and alliteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide meter and stanzaic form to serve the poem's effect; originality can come from novel combinations of familiar line-lengths and feet. Consider how stanzaic arrangement supports rhythmical impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use close circumscription of space as a framing device
rubrics_metrics.description: A close circumscription of space (e.g., a chamber) is 'absolutely necessary to the effect of insulated incident' and acts as a frame concentrating attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a contained locale when you want focus and intensity; framing the action spatially helps maintain unity and concentrate the reader's attention on the intended impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit contrasts to deepen impression
rubrics_metrics.description: Poe uses contrasts—stormy night vs interior serenity, marble bust vs living plumage, fantastic entrance vs later seriousness—to deepen the ultimate impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce physical and tonal contrasts to heighten effects (light/dark, calm/violent, ludicrous/solemn). Plan contrasts to support progression toward the poem's emotional peak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalate incidents/questions to build emotional climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange the lover’s queries so the first is commonplace, then progressively less so, until superstition and despair produce the climactic query answered by the refrain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the sequence of actions or questions to escalate in significance; begin with trivial or ordinary moments and steadily increase stakes and emotional intensity to the predetermined climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce suggestiveness/undercurrent of meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond narrative completeness, 'some amount of suggestiveness—some under-current, however indefinite, of meaning' is required to impart richness and depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Layer an implied, undercurrent meaning or emblematic reading beneath the narrative (e.g., the Raven as emblem of 'Mournful and Never-ending Remembrance') so the work rewards interpretation and lingers with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordinate truth and passion to beauty (use as contrast)
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth and Passion may be introduced but should be 'toned into proper subservience to the predominant aim' (Beauty) and 'enveil[ed]' so as to aid rather than dominate the poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intellectual truth or raw passion are included, integrate them as contrasting elements that enhance rather than distract from the central aesthetic aim; avoid letting them destroy the primary effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity proportional to intensity but allow necessary duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity must be in direct ratio to the intensity of the intended effect, 'with one proviso—that a certain degree of duration is absolutely requisite for the production of any effect at all.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance concision with the minimum duration needed to produce the chosen effect; don't abbreviate so much that the effect cannot mature, nor lengthen so much that unity is lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose sonorous words for thematic and sonic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Poe selected certain words for their sonorousness (e.g., 'Pallas' for the bust's name) and sought sounds (long vowels, resonant consonants) that match the poem's tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select lexis attentive to sound as well as sense; favor words whose phonetic quality reinforces mood, allows emphasis, and fits refrain and meter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan shifts in tone (from fantastic to profound) deliberately
rubrics_metrics.description: Poe deliberately drops the fantastic for a tone of 'the most profound seriousness' at the midpoint to prepare the reader for the dénouement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage tonal transitions carefully: lighter or fantastic material can be used early to disarm or contrast, but shift deliberately into deeper tone when needed to prepare for the climax and ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise, select, and craft mechanically (the artifice of composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poe rejects the myth of ecstatic intuition; composition involves 'cautious selections and rejections... painful erasures and interpolations—the wheels and pinions—the tackle for scene-shifting'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept composition as an engineered process of selection, rejection, and revision. Be willing to excise seemingly good material if it detracts from unity or the intended effect; craft is iterative, not purely spontaneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal moral or emblematic meaning by strategic metaphor
rubrics_metrics.description: Poe uses a metaphor ('Take thy beak from out my heart') and the refrain to 'dispose the mind to seek a moral' and render the Raven emblematic by the poem's close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce metaphorical language at key moments to shift readers from literal to emblematic interpretation; use such moments to make an undercurrent meaning begin to assert itself without explicit exposition.
